papers.title: Deeply-Recursive Convolutional Network for Image Super-Resolution
papers.desc: Introduces DRCN, which applies one convolutional layer recursively up to 16 times and uses recursive supervision plus a skip connection to train a deep image super-resolution model without depth-proportional parameters.

papers.title: Neural GPUs Learn Algorithms
papers.desc: Introduces Neural GPUs, a recurrent convolutional architecture that learns parallel algorithms like addition and multiplication through repeated application of a shared convolutional recurrent block.

papers.title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.desc: Introduces ACT, a deterministic differentiable halting algorithm that lets an RNN learn a variable number of shared state transitions between receiving each input and emitting an output.

papers.title: Reviving and Improving Recurrent Back-Propagation
papers.desc: Revisits recurrent back-propagation for convergent recurrent networks and introduces CG-RBP and Neumann-RBP, with the latter matching truncated BPTT time while using constant memory.

papers.title: Universal Transformers
papers.desc: Introduces the Universal Transformer, which repeatedly applies shared self-attention and transition blocks over depth, optionally with per-position adaptive halting; under the paper's stated assumptions the architecture is Turing-complete.

papers.title: Recurrent Stacking of Layers for Compact Neural Machine Translation Models
papers.desc: Shares one encoder or decoder layer across all stacked depths in neural machine translation, showing that six recurrent applications can approach a six-distinct-layer baseline with far fewer parameters.

papers.title: Trellis Networks for Sequence Modeling
papers.desc: Introduces Trellis Networks, temporal convolutional sequence models that tie weights across depth and inject inputs at every layer, thereby generalizing truncated recurrent networks.

papers.title: Implicit Deep Learning
papers.venue: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
papers.desc: Formulates neural prediction as a learned fixed-point equation and develops well-posed implicit architectures, training schemes, and robustness analysis.

papers.title: Deep Equilibrium Models
papers.desc: Proposes DEQ, which directly solves for the fixed point of an infinite-depth weight-tied network and uses implicit differentiation to train with constant activation memory.

papers.title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
papers.desc: Introduces factorized embeddings and cross-layer parameter sharing to reduce BERT's parameter footprint while retaining or improving performance at larger model scales.

papers.title: Neural Execution of Graph Algorithms
papers.desc: Trains a shared GNN processor to execute graph algorithms step by step, demonstrating benefits from max aggregation and positive transfer between reachability and shortest-path tasks.

papers.title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow
papers.desc: Introduces RAFT, which builds an all-pairs correlation volume and repeatedly applies a learned recurrent update operator to refine a dense optical-flow field.

papers.title: Monotone operator equilibrium networks
papers.desc: Introduces monDEQ, a monotone-operator parameterization and splitting solvers that guarantee a unique, stably computable equilibrium for implicit-depth networks.

papers.title: Multiscale Deep Equilibrium Models
papers.desc: Extends DEQ to synchronized equilibria across multiple feature resolutions, achieving competitive performance on large-scale vision tasks with constant-depth activation memory.

papers.title: Implicit Graph Neural Networks
papers.desc: Defines graph representations as the solution of a learned fixed-point equation, with well-posedness conditions and implicit-differentiation training for long-range graph dependencies.

papers.title: Parameter Efficient Multimodal Transformers for Video Representation Learning
papers.desc: Shares Transformer parameters across depth and modalities, using modality-specific and shared factorization plus low-rank sharing to cut audio-visual video model parameters by up to 97% while enabling end-to-end training.

papers.title: Subformer: Exploring Weight Sharing for Parameter Efficiency in Generative Transformers
papers.desc: Combines sandwich-style cross-layer sharing with self-attentive factorized embeddings to reduce generative Transformer parameters while preserving or improving task performance.

papers.title: Lessons on Parameter Sharing across Layers in Transformers
papers.venue: Fourth Workshop on Simple and Efficient Natural Language Processing (SustaiNLP)
papers.desc: Introduces Sequence, Cycle, and Cycle-reverse strategies for reusing Transformer layers across depth, balancing parameter efficiency, computation time, and translation quality.

papers.title: Can You Learn an Algorithm? Generalizing from Easy to Hard Problems with Recurrent Networks
papers.desc: Shows that recurrent residual networks trained on easy prefix-sum, maze, and chess tasks can solve harder instances by applying their shared block for more iterations at test time.

papers.title: Stabilizing Equilibrium Models by Jacobian Regularization
papers.desc: Regularizes the Jacobian of DEQ update equations to stabilize forward and backward fixed-point solves with minimal additional cost.

papers.title: PonderNet: Learning to Ponder
papers.desc: Introduces a differentiable probabilistic halting objective that learns how many times to apply a recurrent step function for each input.

papers.title: The Neural Data Router: Adaptive Control Flow in Transformers Improves Systematic Generalization
papers.desc: Adds copy gating and geometric attention to a weight-shared Transformer to learn adaptive control flow and improve systematic length and depth generalization.

papers.title: On Training Implicit Models
papers.desc: Proposes phantom gradient, a lightweight backpropagation estimator for implicit (infinite-depth) models that uses damped unrolling and a truncated Neumann series to speed backward passes while matching or surpassing exact-gradient baselines on large-scale tasks.

papers.title: Sliced Recursive Transformer
papers.desc: Builds parameter-efficient vision Transformers by recursively reusing blocks across depth and reducing recursive attention cost with sliced group self-attention.

papers.title: Recurrent Vision Transformer for Solving Visual Reasoning Problems
papers.desc: Introduces RViT, a CNN-Transformer hybrid that shares weights across depth and uses feedback connections to iteratively refine representations for visual same-different reasoning.

papers.title: End-to-end Algorithm Synthesis with Recurrent Networks: Extrapolation without Overthinking
papers.desc: Introduces a recall architecture and progressive training objective that prevent overthinking, enabling shared recurrent networks to extrapolate over thousands of test-time iterations.

papers.title: Deep Equilibrium Optical Flow Estimation
papers.desc: Recasts recurrent optical-flow estimation as an implicit fixed-point layer with analytic differentiation, fixed-point reuse, and sparse correction for lower memory use and faster convergence.

papers.title: Object Representations as Fixed Points: Training Iterative Refinement Algorithms with Implicit Differentiation
papers.desc: Trains iterative object-centric refinement as a fixed-point computation through implicit differentiation, improving SLATE optimization with constant-memory backpropagation.

papers.title: A Generalist Neural Algorithmic Learner
papers.desc: Presents a single shared GNN processor trained jointly across all 30 CLRS algorithmic tasks, with task-specific encoders and decoders and improvements to representations, training, and processor architecture.

papers.title: Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation
papers.desc: Links equilibrium models' ability to benefit from additional inference iterations to path independence and shows that promoting it improves upward generalization.

papers.title: Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers
papers.desc: Constructs a constant-depth looped Transformer that executes one instruction per cycle, using an in-state program counter and reusable instruction blocks to emulate a general-purpose computer, linear algebra routines, and in-context SGD.

papers.title: Sparse Universal Transformer
papers.desc: Combines the Universal Transformer's shared recurrent block with sparse mixtures of experts and stick-breaking halting to reduce compute while preserving compositional generalization.

papers.title: CoTFormer: A Chain-of-Thought Driven Architecture with Budget-Adaptive Computation Cost at Inference
papers.desc: Introduces CoTFormer, which repeatedly applies a shared Transformer block while exposing earlier intermediate representations to later repeats, and uses a learned token router to allocate repeated passes under a chosen inference compute budget.

papers.title: Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms
papers.desc: Proposes an input-injected looped-Transformer architecture and training method for in-context data fitting, matching standard Transformers on the tested function classes with about 1/12 of the parameters while converging to distribution-specific fixed points.

papers.title: Simulation of Graph Algorithms with Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Constructs looped Transformers that simulate major graph algorithms, establishes constant-width Turing completeness, and identifies a finite-precision limit of the construction.

papers.title: AlgoFormer: An Efficient Transformer Framework with Algorithmic Structures
papers.desc: Splits computation into pre-, loop-, and post-transformer stages, showing that structured recurrent depth can outperform standard and vanilla looped transformers on algorithmic and language tasks.

papers.title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers
papers.desc: Introduces MoEUT, a Universal Transformer that recurrently reuses fine-grained MoE layer groups, marginally improving parameter-matched language-modeling perplexity with fewer training MACs and comparable GPU memory to dense Transformers.

papers.title: Looped Transformers for Length Generalization
papers.desc: Introduces an adaptive-step looped Transformer and training procedure that improve length generalization on arithmetic and algorithmic tasks composed from iterative RASP-L operations.

papers.title: On Expressive Power of Looped Transformers: Theoretical Analysis and Enhancement via Timestep Encoding
papers.desc: Derives approximation-rate bounds and an architecture-specific limitation for looped Transformers, then introduces the Timestep-Modulated Looped Transformer (TMLT) to condition per-loop scaling parameters on timestep encodings.

papers.title: Can Looped Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent for In-context Learning?
papers.desc: Proves that trained linear looped Transformers can learn multi-step preconditioned gradient descent for in-context linear regression and establishes convergence of gradient flow to such solutions.

papers.title: Bypassing the Exponential Dependency: Looped Transformers Efficiently Learn In-context by Multi-step Gradient Descent
papers.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
papers.desc: Shows that linear looped Transformers can implement multi-step gradient descent for in-context learning without an exponential dependence of sample size on the number of loops under well-conditioned data.

papers.title: Deep Equilibrium Algorithmic Reasoning
papers.desc: Recasts neural algorithmic reasoning as fixed-point solving with deep-equilibrium GNN processors, removing the need for ground-truth algorithm step counts during training and inference.

papers.title: Relaxed Recursive Transformers: Effective Parameter Sharing with Layer-wise LoRA
papers.desc: Converts pretrained LLMs into compact Recursive and Relaxed Recursive Transformers by repeatedly reusing one block of layers with depth-specific LoRA deltas; simulated oracle-exit results for continuous depth-wise batching suggest a potential 2–3× throughput gain, not a demonstrated deployment speedup.

papers.title: On the Role of Depth and Looping for In-Context Learning with Task Diversity
papers.desc: Analyzes depth for diverse in-context linear-regression tasks, proving matching expressivity for looped Transformers together with stronger distribution-shift robustness and monotonic loss across depth.

papers.title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
papers.desc: Presents Huginn, a 3.5B-parameter recurrent-depth language model trained on 800B tokens whose shared core can be unrolled to variable depth; reasoning performance improves with additional test-time recurrences, and the architecture supports zero-shot adaptive compute and KV-cache sharing.

papers.title: Implicit Language Models are RNNs: Balancing Parallelization and Expressivity
papers.desc: Introduces implicit state-space language models that iterate a shared transition toward a fixed point, recovering RNN-like expressivity while retaining mostly parallel training.

papers.title: Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Studies looped transformers as reasoning models, showing effective-depth scaling, latent-thought simulation of chain-of-thought, and a looping-based regularizer that improves the reasoning-versus-memorization trade-off.

papers.title: Hierarchical Reasoning Model
papers.desc: Proposes HRM, a brain-inspired recurrent architecture with two coupled modules at different timescales: a high-level module for abstract planning and a low-level module for detailed execution.

papers.title: Latent Chain-of-Thought? Decoding the Depth-Recurrent Transformer
papers.desc: Probes a depth-recurrent Transformer to test whether latent chain-of-thought structure emerges across recurrence steps, finding limited evidence and recurrence-depth-dependent interpretability effects.

papers.title: Skip a Layer or Loop it? Test-Time Depth Adaptation of Pretrained LLMs
papers.desc: Proposes Chain-of-Layers (CoLa), an inference-time search method that skips or repeats pretrained LLM layers per sample via MCTS to improve efficiency and reasoning accuracy.

papers.title: Mixture-of-Recursions: Learning Dynamic Recursive Depths for Adaptive Token-Level Computation
papers.desc: Introduces MoR, a recursive Transformer that reuses a shared layer stack while routing each token to a learned recursion depth and restricting attention and KV caching to tokens active at that depth.

papers.title: Beyond Memorization: Extending Reasoning Depth with Recurrence, Memory and Test-Time Compute Scaling
papers.desc: Benchmarks recurrent depth on disjoint-rule cellular automata, finding that layer- and model-level ACT add roughly one effective reasoning step through shared adaptive updates but remain bounded on longer rollouts.

papers.title: Two-Scale Latent Dynamics for Recurrent-Depth Transformers
papers.desc: Analyzes recurrent-depth transformers through a two-scale latent-dynamics lens, showing shrinking and increasingly orthogonal loop updates and deriving a second-order early-exit criterion that improves latency-quality trade-offs.

papers.title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
papers.desc: Proposes Tiny Recursive Model (TRM), which reuses one two-layer network to update a latent state repeatedly and then refine its answer across improvement steps; reports 44.6% on ARC-AGI-1 and 7.8% on ARC-AGI-2 with a 7M-parameter model.

papers.title: Efficient Parallel Samplers for Recurrent-Depth Models
papers.desc: Introduces a diffusion-forcing sampler that advances new tokens while refining their recurrent-depth latent states in parallel, accelerating existing 3.5B looped language models by up to 5x without retraining.

papers.title: Parallel Loop Transformer for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling
papers.desc: Introduces the Parallel Loop Transformer, which preserves looped-model accuracy while reducing latency and memory through cross-loop parallelism and shared-loop KV representations.

papers.title: Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Introduces Ouro, 1.4B and 2.6B pretrained LoopLMs trained on 7.7T tokens; the 1.4B model is comparable to 4B models on most benchmarks, while the 2.6B model outperforms models up to 8B on reasoning-intensive tasks, positioning loop depth as a third scaling axis.

papers.title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
papers.desc: Retrofits pretrained feedforward language models with depth recurrence, preserving performance with less total training compute and achieving better mathematics performance than continued post-training of the feedforward model at a matched compute budget.

papers.title: Think-at-Hard: Selective Latent Iterations to Improve Reasoning Language Models
papers.desc: Introduces Think-at-Hard, a dynamic latent-thinking method that uses a learned decider to apply extra recurrent latent iterations only to hard tokens, with LoRA refiners and duo-causal attention across iteration depth.

papers.title: Universal Reasoning Model
papers.desc: Proposes URM, a Universal Transformer-based architecture with weight tying that beats standard transformers on reasoning benchmarks through iterative depth computation.

papers.title: Depth-Recurrent Attention Mixtures: Giving Latent Reasoning the Attention it Deserves
papers.desc: Introduces Dreamer, a depth-recurrent attention-mixture framework combining sequence, depth, and sparse expert attention, and reports higher reasoning accuracy and data efficiency than tightly FLOP-, parameter-, and memory-matched baselines.

papers.title: On the Role of Computation in Reinforcement Learning
papers.desc: Formalizes compute-bounded RL policies and introduces a minimal variable-compute architecture, showing that extra iterative computation improves performance and longer-horizon generalization across 31 online and offline RL tasks.

papers.title: Recurrent-Depth VLA: Implicit Test-Time Compute Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models via Latent Iterative Reasoning
papers.desc: Introduces RD-VLA, a vision-language-action architecture with a weight-tied recurrent action head and adaptive stopping, enabling latent test-time compute scaling for robotics with constant memory footprint.

papers.title: Understanding Dynamic Compute Allocation in Recurrent Transformers
papers.desc: Uses ANIRA as a controlled recurrent-Transformer framework to study per-token variable-depth computation, showing that adaptive compute can align with token complexity while failing to extrapolate to longer algorithmic inputs.

papers.title: Looping Back to Move Forward: Recursive Transformers for Efficient and Flexible Large Multimodal Models
papers.desc: Introduces RecursiveVLM, a recursive multimodal transformer with a recursive connector and monotonic recursion loss that enables on-demand extra refinement under varying compute budgets.

papers.title: Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Introduces RLTT, a reinforcement-learning objective that assigns reward across the full latent thought trajectory of looped language models rather than only the final latent state.

papers.title: LoopFormer: Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning via Shortcut Modulation
papers.desc: Introduces LoopFormer, trained on variable-length trajectories with shortcut-consistency regularization to enable budget-conditioned reasoning and stable internal trajectories across loop depths.

papers.title: SpiralFormer: Looped Transformers Can Learn Hierarchical Dependencies via Multi-Resolution Recursion
papers.desc: Introduces SpiralFormer, a looped transformer that applies shared layers under a multi-resolution recursion schedule to learn hierarchical dependencies more efficiently than fixed-resolution recurrent baselines.

papers.title: AdaPonderLM: Gated Pondering Language Models with Token-Wise Adaptive Depth
papers.desc: Introduces AdaPonderLM, a self-supervised recurrent language model with token-wise halting gates and KV reuse, allocating more loop steps to hard tokens under a fixed compute budget.

papers.title: Mixture of Universal Experts: Scaling Virtual Width via Depth-Width Transformation
papers.desc: Proposes MOUE, which reuses a universal layer-agnostic expert pool across layers to transform depth into virtual width and improve MoE performance under fixed activation budgets.

papers.title: Recursive Inference Machines for Neural Reasoning
papers.desc: Introduces Recursive Inference Machines, a nested generator-solver framework that subsumes TRMs; RIMformer reweights full reasoning histories for ARC-AGI and Sudoku, while TabRIM applies recursive inference to tabular classification.

papers.title: Tiny Autoregressive Recursive Models
papers.desc: Studies compute placement in autoregressive Transformers under matched block-pass budgets, finding that untied depth and flat two-stream recurrence perform best on small character-level algorithmic tasks while the full Autoregressive TRM provides no consistent benefit.

papers.title: Adaptive Loops and Memory in Transformers: Think Harder or Know More?
papers.desc: Introduces transformers with adaptive per-layer looping and gated memory banks, showing that combining learned halting with extra storage improves reasoning under matched parameter and FLOP budgets.

papers.title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Proposes LoopRPT, a reinforcement pre-training method for looped language models that assigns learning signals to latent iterations, improving accuracy-compute trade-offs and strengthening early-stage reasoning on Ouro.

papers.title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
papers.desc: Introduces a depth-recurrent Transformer for compositional generalization, with silent thinking, LayerScale, and identity-biased recurrence enabling stable deep latent iteration.

papers.title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers
papers.desc: Studies implicit reasoning in recurrent-depth transformers, showing that iterating shared transformer layers can unlock systematic generalization and depth extrapolation while also exposing overthinking limits.

papers.title: ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation
papers.desc: Introduces Elastic Looped Transformers for image and video generation, using weight-shared recurrent transformer blocks plus Intra-Loop Self Distillation to support any-time inference with dynamic quality-compute trade-offs from a single training run.

papers.title: Relational Preference Encoding in Looped Transformer Internal States
papers.desc: Probes frozen Ouro loop states with lightweight evaluators on HH-RLHF, finding that preference labels are primarily decodable from pairwise state differences; the authors frame this as an internal-consistency probe of Ouro's learned value organization rather than direct prediction of noisy human annotations.

papers.title: A Deep Equilibrium Network for Hyperspectral Unmixing
papers.desc: Recasts hyperspectral unmixing as a deep equilibrium model, replacing the reconstruction-gradient operator with a trainable convolutional update and solving for an implicit fixed point with constant-memory differentiation.

papers.title: A Mechanistic Analysis of Looped Reasoning Language Models
papers.desc: Mechanistically analyzes explicit cyclic recurrence in looped language models, finding that many studied models approach layer-specific cyclic fixed points and that recurrent blocks repeatedly reproduce feedforward-like stages of inference, while also documenting non-convergent cases.

papers.title: Parcae: Scaling Laws For Stable Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Introduces Parcae, a stable looped language model that constrains injection spectral norms to prevent instability and studies isoFLOPs-style training- and test-time scaling laws for quality gains under fixed-parameter budgets.

papers.title: Hierarchical vs. Flat Iteration in Shared-Weight Transformers
papers.desc: Empirically compares two-speed hierarchical shared-weight recurrence with flat shared-weight iteration and independent-layer Transformers, finding a robust 3.4-nat validation-CE advantage over a parameter-matched Universal Transformer while reporting caveats for the independent-layer comparisons.

papers.title: Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Analyzes stability and generalization in looped transformers through a fixed-point framework, characterizing when recall and normalization yield reachable, input-dependent, and trainable loop dynamics.

papers.title: LASER: Low-Rank Activation SVD for Efficient Recursion
papers.desc: Analyzes TRM activation geometry during recursive unrolling and introduces LASER, a dynamic low-rank compression method for stored training activations that reduces activation memory by about 60% without statistically significant accuracy loss.

papers.title: One Step Forward and K Steps Back: Better Reasoning with Denoising Recursion Models
papers.desc: Introduces Denoising Recursion Models, a looped-transformer training method that corrupts targets and trains recursive refinement over multiple steps, improving ARC-AGI reasoning over TRM.

papers.title: How Much Is One Recurrence Worth? Iso-Depth Scaling Laws for Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Measures the parameter value of recurrence in looped language models with iso-depth scaling laws, estimating how extra recurrent passes trade off against unique depth and training compute.

papers.title: Hyperloop Transformers
papers.desc: Introduces Hyperloop Transformers, a parameter-efficient looped Transformer that applies only a middle block recurrently and adds hyper-connections between loops to improve memory-efficient language modeling.

papers.title: Universal Transformers Need Memory: Depth-State Trade-offs in Adaptive Recursive Reasoning
papers.desc: Studies a single-block Universal Transformer with ACT on Sudoku-Extreme, showing that learned memory tokens are necessary for non-trivial recursive-depth reasoning and that ACT initialization can trap the model in shallow computation.

papers.title: On Halting vs Converging in Recurrent Graph Neural Networks
papers.desc: Analyzes recurrent graph neural networks that repeatedly apply message passing until convergence or halting, proving expressiveness relationships between converging, output-converging, and halting RGNN variants.

papers.title: ITS-Mina: A Harris Hawks Optimization-Based All-MLP Framework with Iterative Refinement and External Attention for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
papers.desc: Applies a shared-parameter iterative refinement module inside an all-MLP multivariate time-series forecasting system, using the loop-model pattern for a concrete forecasting application.

papers.title: Visual Implicit Autoregressive Modeling
papers.desc: Introduces VIAR, replacing the deep middle stack of a visual autoregressive generator with an implicit equilibrium layer trained by Jacobian-Free Backpropagation and controlled by per-scale iteration budgets at inference.

papers.title: RD-ViT: Recurrent-Depth Vision Transformer for Semantic Segmentation with Reduced Data Dependence Extending the Recurrent-Depth Transformer Architecture to Dense Prediction
papers.desc: Introduces RD-ViT, looping one shared Transformer block for dense 2D and 3D segmentation with stable input injection, adaptive halting, depth-wise LoRA, and optional MoE specialization.

papers.title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models
papers.desc: Analyzes layerwise inference dynamics in tabular foundation models and uses the observed depth redundancy to build a looped single-layer model that preserves comparable performance with about 20% of the original parameters.

papers.title: Transformers Efficiently Perform In-Context Logistic Regression via Normalized Gradient Descent
papers.desc: Proves that softmax transformers can implement in-context logistic regression by treating layers as normalized-gradient-descent steps, then trains one self-attention layer and applies it recurrently as a looped model with convergence and OOD guarantees.

papers.title: Bifurcation Models: Learning Set-Valued Solution Maps with Weight-Tied Dynamics
papers.desc: Studies weight-tied dynamics for set-valued solution maps, proving that regular equilibrium dynamics can represent multiple branches; experiments discover multiple low-energy Ising equilibria, while Allen-Cahn requires explicit diversity promotion and exhibits an accuracy-diversity tradeoff.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Looped Transformer: Decoupling Compute from Memory in Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Introduces MELT, which maintains one fixed-size KV cache per layer across recurrent reasoning loops, updates it through learned gating, and adapts pretrained Ouro models with chunk-wise two-phase training to keep cache memory independent of loop depth.

papers.title: Sparse Layers are Critical to Scaling Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Shows that MoE-style sparse layers can make looped language models scale better than dense looped transformers, with routing divergence across repeated shared layers recovering expressivity and loop boundaries serving as effective early-exit points.

papers.title: Quantum Injection Pathways for Implicit Graph Neural Networks
papers.desc: Formulates quantum-signal injection pathways for graph deep-equilibrium models, comparing fixed, state-dependent, and backbone-dependent coupling inside the fixed-point operator with contraction guarantees and graph-classification experiments.

papers.title: LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models
papers.desc: Converts pretrained LLMs into encoder, looped reasoning block, and decoder components, using selective gating, random deep supervision, and adaptive early exiting to stabilize latent looping without training recurrent models from scratch.

papers.title: Solve the Loop: Attractor Models for Language and Reasoning
papers.desc: Introduces Attractor Models, where a backbone proposes output embeddings and an attractor module iteratively solves a fixed point with implicit differentiation, improving looped language modeling and small-model reasoning while allowing adaptive convergence-depth inference.
